target: AG1's claim that alternative energies can effectively replace fossil fuels because some countries already have very high renewable electricity shares
objection: A few countries with high renewable electricity shares do not prove that alternative energies can effectively replace fossil fuels at large-country scale, especially because the United States has never historically exceeded 20% alternative-energy use.

target: AG1's assumption that electricity generation data alone shows fossil fuels can be replaced
objection: Fossil fuels are used for much more than electricity; they also power transportation and industrial heat, so high renewable electricity shares do not by themselves demonstrate a full replacement of fossil fuels.

target: AG1's reliance on renewable electricity examples as evidence that the transition is achievable
objection: Alternative energies alone cannot provide the firm, dispatchable low-carbon capacity needed to fully displace fossil fuels; an effective net-zero pathway requires continued natural-gas use as a bridge fuel.

target: AG1's claim that nuclear energy can help replace fossil fuels
objection: Nuclear energy is too dangerous and ineffective to be a serious global-warming solution, because accidents like Fukushima erase carbon-free electricity gains.

target: AG1's reply that U.S. low alternative-energy penetration does not prove impossibility
objection: The United States is a large, high-capacity energy system that should have adopted scalable alternatives if they could work at scale, so its long-term ceiling of under 20% indicates intrinsic scalability limits that likely generalize to other large countries.

target: AG1's claim that nuclear can accelerate fossil-fuel replacement
objection: Even if nuclear is low-carbon, it cannot be treated as a dependable accelerator because it cannot provide always-available electricity; periodic refueling, maintenance outages, and other disruptions mean nuclear plus renewables cannot guarantee firm power at all times.

target: AG1's claim that electrification and firm nuclear-backed power can replace fossil fuels across the whole economy
objection: Replacing fossil fuels requires more than low-carbon electricity: major end uses like transportation fuels and industrial heat also must be decarbonized, so an electricity-focused strategy does not establish whole-economy replacement.

target: AG1's argument that hydrogen and synthetic fuels made from clean electricity can decarbonize transport and heat
objection: Making hydrogen or e-fuels from electricity wastes energy through conversion losses, so an alternative-energy-only e-fuels strategy would require vastly more low-carbon electricity than the fossil energy it replaces.

target: AG1's claim that fossil-fuel feedstock use can be replaced with CO2-based chemistry and non-fossil carbon sources
objection: Chemical manufacturing still needs non-fossil carbon inputs at very large scale, and the necessary capture/removal capacity cannot be assumed to be built quickly enough to displace fossil feedstocks nationwide.
